notes: Mail-handling totals are lower bounds since 2026-11-14. Seeded from: (1) 19 redacted corpus samples (7 phishing, 10 spam, 2 ads; 15 Gmail, 4 Outlook), which represent mail actually reviewed and recorded; (2) a complete read-only count of clearly unsolicited casino or gambling mail in Outlook Deleted Items dated 13-15 November 2026 (11 messages still in Deleted Items, of which 2 were already corpus samples, plus 1 further casino message from 15 November that was permanently deleted rather than moved to Deleted Items). Unique blocked senders start at the 19 distinct corpus sender addresses (the handling procedure blocks the exact sender of each clear phishing or spam message). Blocked domains are the 4 already listed on campaign.repeated-malicious-sender-domain.v1 (two observed on Gmail campaigns, two on Outlook casino mail). Phishing reports equal the 7 corpus phishing samples (phishing is reported to the provider). movedToTrash is 28 because it excludes that one permanently deleted Outlook message. Gmail Trash in the same period also held further campaign mail, but a complete classified count was not possible (search results include unrelated trash and are capped at 50 threads per query), so those extras are not included. Uncertain and legitimate counts start at 0 because only handled junk was recorded. mailsChecked equals the sum of the categorised counts. spamChecksRun is 3 (the 14 November review, the 15 November morning check, and the 15 November Outlook casino cleanup). Per-provider check counts count only runs that recorded handling in that mailbox (Gmail 2, Outlook 2). lastCheck is the time the rules from that last cleanup were merged.
